text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000252's 99215 rate runs well above peers at every complexity level, but only two 99215 charts were reviewed, too few to say whether the level is supported.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevation does not look like a sicker panel. In the by-complexity table this provider's 99215 share is roughly two to three times the all-provider share in every stratum, including patients with 0 or 1 conditions. The low-complexity sample shows 99215s on single-symptom visits such as back pain (M54.50), urinary infection (N39.0) and abdominal pain (R10.9), for example C0129314, C0129460 and C0129499. Against that, both documented 99215s (C0129515 and C0129709) were documented at high MDM with about 40 minutes, and no billed level was documented below what was billed. The documentation is far too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding, and C0129515 deserves attention: it is a 0-condition back-pain visit documented as high MDM, which could be a genuinely complex encounter or an inflated or templated note. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 sample, starting with the 0-condition symptom visits, and check the notes for cloned or templated MDM language, including the 2 data-reviewed notes with no lab or test line on the claim."}
